page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v5 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the DLDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 64.0 GB of system memory, which equates to a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the server is equipped with a bundled 1229 GB SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for most general compute tasks, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1674.0 and a multi-core score of 14190.0. It demonstrates strong performance in specific workloads, such as Geekbench image processing at 13882.0 and text generation for small 135M LLM models at 300.04 tokens per second. However, memory-intensive operations and large-scale LLM inference show clear limitations; prompt processing for a 70B model drops to a weak 6.66 tokens per second, and text generation falls to a poor 2.29 tokens per second, reflecting the constraints of its 64.0 GB memory capacity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32lds_v5 offers a specialized hardware profile that trades off memory capacity to provide a higher density of dedicated compute cores and substantial local SSD storage. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective option for workloads that require high CPU throughput and fast local disk access but do not demand massive RAM arrays. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, web serving, image processing, and database operations that fit comfortably within the 64.0 GB memory limit.
description: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v5 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 64.0 GB of memory and a bundled 1229 GB local SSD. Benchmark results indicate average performance across standard compute metrics, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 14190.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 36820.34. It exhibits strong capabilities in image processing and small-model LLM text generation, though it struggles with large-scale LLM inference due to its low memory-to-CPU ratio. This server is qualitatively cost-effective for compute-heavy tasks with moderate memory requirements, making it well-suited for software compilation, static web serving, and database operations.
